correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the entire vertex census from the box/equality rank condition: at most one free coordinate, and 0<t<1 excludes interior z. Two orbits A(z=0,k Boolean ones) and B(z=t,k−1 ones and one 1−t) are exhaustive. Strictly convex squared covering objective and S_m symmetry reduce every possible center in the inherited affine hyperplane to c(u)=((k−u)/m repeated,u). Direct algebra gives D_A=k(m−k)/m+(m+1)u²/m and D_B−D_A=2t(t−(m−k)/m)−2t(m+1)u/m. The minimum of max(D_A,D_B) is u=0 below threshold, or their intersection u=[mt−(m−k)]/(m+1) above; the left curve is decreasing until that intersection and the right curve increasing. This yields unique center, radius, exact B clearance 2t((m−k)/m−t) below threshold, all contacts thereafter, and one-sided second-derivative jump 2m/(m+1). At t→1 the ordinary hypersimplex radius is recovered; endpoints are excluded for orbit counting. Independently replicated 75 small rational cases, which do not prove the universal real-parameter theorem.
